description: In the Odyssey, Odysseus confronts the Cyclops Polyphemus. His  saves him, but his pride attracts the wrath of Poseidon. [[metis]]

hero.hook: A one-eyed giant devours his men. Odysseus cannot win by force. So he invents a name: Nobody.

blocks.text: After the Trojan War, **Ulysses**, king of the island of Ithaca, tries to return home. Homer recounts his journey in the **Odyssey**. In song IX, he approaches a fertile island where the [[Cyclopes]], solitary giants with one eye, live.

There he meets **Polyphemus**, son of the sea god **Poseidon**. The episode isn't just a monster tale. It's a lesson: , cunning intelligence, can beat brute force. But , excessive pride, can ruin everything. [[metis]] [[hubris]]

Ulysses arrives with twelve companions. The Cyclops have no assemblies, no laws, no real agriculture. They live in caves. The Greeks believe in the [[xenia]]: the sacred duty to welcome strangers, under the protection of Zeus.

blocks.caption: Polyphemus, the Cyclops, figure of lawless force.

blocks.text: In the cave, the men see cheeses and cattle. The companions want to leave. Odysseus insists on waiting for the master, hoping for a host gift. Error. Polyphemus returns, blocks the entrance with an immense rock, and devours two Greeks. Strength will not be enough. You have to be cunning.

Odysseus cuts an olive stake, wood dear to Athena, goddess of wisdom. He hides it. Then he offers Polyphemus a very strong, almost pure wine. The giant gets drunk. Before falling asleep, he asks the name of his guest.
In Greek, Ulysses says his name is **Outis**, “Nobody”. This word also evokes **métis**, cunning. Homer plays on the double meaning: it is indeed the ruse that defeats the giant.

blocks.caption: Odysseus and his men blind Polyphemus, a famous scene from Greek vases.

blocks.text: Ulysses replies: “My name is **Person**. » Then his men drive the burning stake into the single eye. The other Cyclops come running. “Who is killing you? » they ask. " Person ! » replies Polyphemus. They walk away, thinking of divine evil.

The next day, blind Polyphemus guards the exit. He feels the back of each sheep. Ulysses ties his companions under the bellies of the woolliest animals. He himself hangs under the largest ram. The giant caresses the animal without feeling the enemy just below.

Once at sea, Ulysses cannot resist. He shouts his true name, his lineage, his city. He wants the [[kleos]], the glory that lives on in name. Polyphemus can finally curse a specific target with his father Poseidon.

Polyphemus prays to Poseidon: that Ulysses never arrives home, or else late, alone, after having lost all his companions. This curse structures the ten years of wandering that follow. The sea becomes a punishment.

blocks.caption: Poseidon, god of the sea, avenges his son Polyphemus.

blocks.text: The myth opposes two heroisms. In the Iliad, one wins through strength and fame. In the Odyssey, we survive through restraint. Odysseus won through wit. He lost through the pride of wanting to be recognized.
Faced with Polyphemus, Ulysses triumphs thanks to the [[metis]] and the name “Person”. By revealing his identity for, he triggers Poseidon's anger and prolongs his exile. [[kleos]]
